roadmap.title: IELTS Roadmap
roadmap.headline: A structured five-stage preparation roadmap from baseline diagnosis to exam-day mastery.
roadmap.subheadline: Eliminate random preparation. Follow clear stage gates that connect diagnostic checks, core foundation building, skill clinics, timed simulation exams, and target band readiness.
roadmap.purposeTitle: What IELTS Roadmap Is Designed to Solve
roadmap.purposeBody: Most candidates spend months hopping between disconnected video clips and isolated mock PDFs without knowing which skill criteria actually hold back their overall band. The IELTS Roadmap organizes your entire timeline into measurable stages tied directly to diagnostic accuracy and official band descriptors.

sampleDialogs.studentQuestion: Why did my Task 2 Coherence stay at 6.0 even when I used linking words?
sampleDialogs.coachReply: Examiners look for logical progression inside the ideas themselves—not mechanical openers like 'Firstly' or 'Moreover' at every line. Your second body paragraph introduces economic cost without connecting back to your thesis on public transit access. Start paragraph 2 with a clear referencing phrase linking back to that idea, then develop one concrete example.

sampleDialogs.studentQuestion: I keep running out of things to say at 70 seconds during Part 2 cue cards.
sampleDialogs.coachReply: Instead of stretching bullet 1 for too long, split your 60-second scratchpad cleanly across 4 zones: Setting (15s), Action Steps (40s), Challenge/Feeling (35s), and Future Outcome (30s). Even if a prompt only lists four bullets, adding one concrete reflection guarantees effortless two-minute pacing.

sampleDialogs.studentQuestion: I always score 11/13 in Passage 1, then rush and miss half of Passage 3.
sampleDialogs.coachReply: Passage 3 carries denser academic inference and multiple-choice traps, yet many candidates spend 24 minutes chasing perfection on Passage 1. Set hard checkpoints: finish Passage 1 at 17:00 elapsed, Passage 2 at 36:00, leaving 24 full minutes for Passage 3.

criteria.name: Task Response
criteria.note: Addresses both views briefly; conclusion repeats earlier points rather than synthesizing.

criteria.name: Coherence & Cohesion
criteria.note: Clear paragraph breaks, though mechanical openers ('Firstly', 'Besides') appear repeatedly.

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.note: Adequate meaning communicated, with reliance on general words ('good', 'problem', 'people').

criteria.name: Grammatical Range
criteria.note: Mix of simple and compound sentences; occasional article and comma-splice slips.

bandSamples.upgradeTip: State your explicit stance in the opening introduction and replace broad claims in Body 2 with one grounded causal example.

criteria.name: Task Response
criteria.note: Presents a clear, well-supported position throughout with balanced main ideas.

criteria.name: Coherence & Cohesion
criteria.note: Logical progression overall; one abrupt transition between housing and transit sub-points.

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.note: Natural academic collocations ('mitigate congestion', 'urban sprawl') with rare minor slips.

criteria.name: Grammatical Range
criteria.note: Frequent error-free complex structures and accurate conditional clauses.

bandSamples.upgradeTip: Tighten the opening concession bridge of Paragraph 3 using referencing pronouns to elevate Coherence to 7.5.

criteria.name: Task Response
criteria.note: Fully developed, nuanced argument addressing subtleties and counter-considerations cleanly.

criteria.name: Coherence & Cohesion
criteria.note: Seamless topic sentences and organic lexical chaining make paragraph boundaries effortless.

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.note: Flexible, idiomatic academic register with precise collocation awareness.

criteria.name: Grammatical Range
criteria.note: Wide repertoire of inversion, non-finite clauses, and crisp punctuation control.

bandSamples.upgradeTip: Maintain concise word choice (~290 words) so depth remains sharp without drifting off-focus under time limits.
